versions.name: Taught, first round
versions.note: 60,000 examples in 35 families, through the whole-number spec

challenges.question: Print the capital letter A. There is no input.
Print ABC. There is no input.
Read one character and print it. If more input follows, leave it alone.
Read one character and print it two times.
Read one letter and print the letter that follows it in the alphabet. The input is never z or Z.
Read two characters and print them in the opposite order.
Print Hi. There is no input.
Print Hello, World! exactly: with the comma, the space and the exclamation mark, and no line break at the end. There is no input.
Print the 26 capital letters from A to Z. There is no input.
Print the digits 9876543210. There is no input.
Print twenty stars: ********************. There is no input.
Print all 95 characters with the numbers 32 to 126, in order: it starts with a space and !"# and ends with |}~. There is no input.
Print five lines of stars: one star on the first line, two on the second, up to five. End every line, also the last, with a line break (character 10). There is no input.
Print the whole input, unchanged. The input can be empty. It never holds the character with number 0.
The input is one or more lines, and every line ends with a line break (character 10). Print the first line, without its line break.
Print the input without its first character. The input can be empty.
Print the first, third, fifth, ... character of the input. abcdef becomes ace. The input can be empty.
Print every character of the input two times: abc becomes aabbcc. The input can be empty.
Print only the last character of the input. If the input is empty, print nothing.
The input has at most 9 characters. Print how many there are, as one digit: hello gives 5.
Read two digits and print their sum, which is never more than 9: 34 gives 7.
Read two digits. The first is never smaller than the second. Print the first minus the second: 83 gives 5.
Read one digit and print that many stars: 3 gives ***, and 0 gives nothing.
Read one digit and count down from it to 0: 3 gives 3210.
Read two digits and print their product, which is never more than 9: 24 gives 8.
Read one digit and print half of it, rounded down: 6 gives 3 and 7 gives 3.
Read one character and print its number in ordinary digits: A gives 65. If the input is empty, print 0.
The input is a number from 32 to 126, written in digits. Print the character with that number: 65 gives A.
Print the input backwards: hello becomes olleh. The input can be empty and never holds the character with number 0.
The input is made of small letters a to z only. Print it in capitals: hello becomes HELLO. The input can be empty.
Print the input followed by an exclamation mark: hello becomes hello!. On an empty input print only !.
Print the whole input two times in a row: abc becomes abcabc. The input can be empty and never holds the character with number 0.
Print the input followed by the input backwards: abc becomes abccba. The input can be empty and never holds the character with number 0.
Swap every two characters: abcdef becomes badcfe. If one character is left over at the end, print it as it is: abc becomes bac. The input never holds the character with number 0.
Print the input between square brackets: loop becomes [loop]. On an empty input print [].
The input is made of small letters a to z only. Replace every letter by the next one in the alphabet, and z by a: buzz becomes cvaa. The input can be empty.
Print Y if the input holds at least one character, and N if it is empty.
Read one digit. Print Z if it is 0, and N if it is not.
Read two characters. Print = if they are the same, and ! if they differ.
Print E if the number of characters in the input is even, and O if it is odd. An empty input has 0 characters, which is even.
Print the input with every space replaced by an underscore _: a b c becomes a_b_c. All other characters stay as they are.
Print the input without its spaces: a b c becomes abc.
Read two digits and print the larger of the two: 38 gives 8. If they are equal, print that digit once.
Print how many times the small letter a occurs in the input, as one digit. It occurs at most 9 times: banana gives 3.
Print A without using the command + anywhere. There is no input.

Brainfuck interpreters do not agree on what , does when the input has run out. Some put 0 in the cell, some put 255, and some leave the cell as it was. Write a program that copies the input and stops,

Print the number of characters in the input in ordinary digits: an input of 300 characters gives 300. The input has at most 1,000 characters and can be empty (print 0). The cells here are 16 bit: they
Print the input with every small letter a to z made a capital. Everything else stays as it is: Hi, there! becomes HI, THERE!.
Read one character and print its number as eight binary digits, highest first: A (65) gives 01000001.
Read two digits and print their product in ordinary digits: 67 gives 42 and 99 gives 81.

The input is made of the characters [ and ] only, at most 100 of them. Print Y if it could be the brackets of a correct brainfuck program: every [ has its own ] further on. Otherwise print N. So [[][]

blind.question: Make a program that outputs the word "brainfuck".
Output an exclamation mark followed by a question mark. Nothing is read.
Write out the digits 0 through 9 in increasing order.
Output fifteen equals signs in a row.
Show the lowercase alphabet from a to z.
Produce three lines, each containing four hash signs (#), every line ending in a newline.
Print the letters Z, Y, X, W, V in that order.
Output the text OK followed by a newline.
Print 7 at signs: @@@@@@@
Print a staircase of plus signs: 1 on the first line up to 4 on the fourth, each line ending with a newline.
Echo whatever is typed in, without changes.
Output the first character you read three times in a row.
Read a single character and output the character right after it in ASCII.
Drop the first two characters of the input and print what remains.
Read three characters and output them in reverse.
Output every input character twice in a row.
Print only the very last character of what you read. Print nothing for empty input.
Print characters from the input until you hit a comma, not including the comma. There is always a comma.
Print the first three characters of the input; it is always at least three long.
The input is two digits. Output their sum as a single digit (it never exceeds 9).
Read two digits, a then b, with a >= b, and output a - b.
Read one digit and output double its value; the answer stays below 10.
Given a digit, print that many dashes.
Read a digit n and output all digits from n down to 0.
Read a digit and output it plus 3; the result is at most 9.
Input: two digits. Output: the product, which is at most 9.
Read a digit and print the remainder when it is divided by 3.
Two digits come in. Print their sum written in decimal, which may need two digits.
Print how many characters the input contains, in decimal. The input has at most 200 characters.
Read one character and print its ASCII code in decimal.
Input: two digits. Print the smaller one.
Read a digit and print it divided by 4, rounded down.
Turn the input around so the last character comes first.
Convert every lowercase letter of the input (all lowercase a-z) to uppercase.
Print the input, then a period.
Wrap the input in curly braces: hi becomes {hi}.
Swap neighbouring characters pairwise; a leftover last character stays.
Repeat the entire input two times.
Shift each letter one back in the alphabet; the input only uses b to z.
Print the input and then the same input reversed.
The input is lowercase letters. Print it with each letter moved forward one place, z wrapping around to a.
Print the input with all exclamation marks removed.
Print 1 if there is any input at all, otherwise print 0.
Read a character; print T if it is an x and F otherwise.
Read two characters and output S when they match and D when they do not.
Output Y when the input length is odd and N when it is even.
Replace each comma in the input with a semicolon.
Count the letter e in the input and print the count as one digit (at most 9).
Read two digits and print the larger.
The input consists of ( and ) only. Print Y if every bracket is properly closed, N otherwise.
Read a number written in decimal digits (between 33 and 126) and print the character with that code.
Print the input followed by its length as one digit. The input has at most 9 characters.
Print the input reversed and in capitals. The input is lowercase letters only.
Print each character of the input followed by a space.
Print every character of the input on its own line.
Print the sum of all digits in the input, in decimal. The input is only digits.
Read a digit and print that many lines with a single star each.
Print the alphabet backwards, from z to a.
Print the input without its last character.
Read a character and print the character two places after it, twice.

families.question: Write a program to print the capital letter R. No input.
Print "K" 40 times. There is no input.
Write a program to print UTSRQ. No input.
In brainfuck, print 7 lines of stars: one on the first line, two on the second, up to seven. End every line with a line break.
Write a brainfuck program to copy the input to the output.
Read one character and print it.
In brainfuck, read one character and print the character 5 places earlier in the ASCII table.
Using brainfuck, read 4 characters and print them in reverse order.
Print the input without its first character.
Write a program to print every character of the input 5 times.
Print the first character of the input and then every fourth one after it: `abcdefghij` becomes `aei`.
Brainfuck: print the first two characters of the input. The input has at least 2 characters.
Write a program to the input contains ','. Print everything before the first `,`.
Print how many times 'u' occurs in the input, as one digit. It occurs at most 9 times.
Print one "=" for every character of the input. The input can be empty.
Read one digit and print it minus 7. The digit is never smaller than 7.
Read three digits and print their sum, which is never more than 9: `123` gives `6`.
Read a digit and print 3 times that digit, which is at most 9.
Write a brainfuck program to read one digit and print that many `=`'s: 3 gives "===", and `0` gives nothing.
Read one digit and count up from 0 to it: `3` gives `0123`.
Write a brainfuck program to read one digit, at least 1, and count down from it to 1: "3" gives 321.
Write a program to print the input backwards: `abc` becomes `cba`. It never holds the character 0.
Print the input followed by the input backwards. It never holds the character 0.
Print the whole input two times in a row. It never holds the character 0.
Brainfuck: the input is made of small letters only. Print it in capitals.
Print the input with every character 3 places later in the ASCII table. The input may be empty.
Brainfuck: print the input between '{' and `}`: `hi` becomes `{hi}`.
Print the input followed by "?".
Swap every two characters of the input. If one is left over at the end, print it as it is.
Print "T" if the input holds at least one character, and "F" if it is empty.
Using brainfuck, read one character. Print `T` if it is 'Q', and 'F' if it is not.
Read two characters. Print '1' if they are the same, and '0' if they differ.
In brainfuck, print "e" if the number of characters in the input is even, and "o" if it is odd. An empty input counts as even.
Brainfuck: print the input with every `e` replaced by _. All other characters stay as they are.
Print the input without its "," characters.
Using brainfuck, read the whole input and print its last character (nothing if it is empty).
Print the length of the input as a single digit. It has at most 5 characters.
Count the characters of the input and print the count in decimal (at most 255).
Write a brainfuck program to read two digits and print their sum, which is never more than 9.
Write a program to multiply the two digits of the input and print the product in decimal, which can have two digits.
Brainfuck: read one digit and print it divided by 5, rounded down.
Read one character and print its number in ordinary digits: A gives 65. If the input is empty, print 0.
Write a brainfuck program to read a number in decimal digits and print the character with that ASCII code (32 to 126).
Write a brainfuck program to read one digit and count down from it to 0.
Move every small letter of the input one place on in the alphabet, z going round to a. The input may be empty.
Write a program to print `o` without using the command + anywhere.
The input is made of the characters [ and ] only. Print "Y" if the brackets match, and "N" if they do not.
